note: How a piece is performed (doc 24, Realizing a piece). beat: compound meters (6/8, 9/8, 12/8) count the dotted quarter as the beat, others the quarter; a piece's tempo range is in those beats per minute. rubato (per phrase, x from 0 to 1 across it): t(x) = base x (1 + push x sin(pi x)) x (1 - rit x smoothstep(0.8, 1, x)); push up to pushMax faster toward the middle, rit between ritMin and ritMax slower into the cadence (finalRit at the very end); fermata holds a marked note this many times longer, plus fermataGapS of silence after it. humanize: onset jitter up to jitterMs either way, the melody this many ms ahead on downbeats (melodyLeadMs, doc 24: about 8), velocity jitter up to velJitter either way. dynamics: the velocity of each dynamic mark, and accompanimentOffset (velocity below the melody's), counterOffset, padOffset. phraseArch: up to this much louder toward a phrase's middle. pedal: legato pedaling, lifting liftBeforeS before each chord change and pressing pressAfterS after it, released finalReleaseS after the last note ends. roll: a rolled chord spreads its notes this far apart (rollMs) and ornament chance rolls the final chord. patterns: how a generated accompaniment plays a chord: sustained (all at once, held), slow-roll (bass, then the upper notes rolled upward), broken-8ths (bass on the beat, then the upper notes in eighths, up and back), open-fifth-offbeat (left hand root and fifth held, a dyad on each offbeat), pad-only (the pad holds the chord, no piano accompaniment); each pattern names its voicing style from recipes/music/voicing.json. pad: when a palette brings the pad in, it holds each chord's upper voices this many semitones down (octaveDown) at padOffset.
